data.body:
DENIED-ACCESS DRILL AGAINST THE LIVE BOT — all four observations, stated separately as the criterion requires.

SCOPE DECISION, taken with the operator rather than unilaterally, because this drill's blast radius differs in KIND from the earlier one. An IAM denial produces gap_reason 'llm-unavailable', which is in adapter.RETRYABLE_GAP_REASONS, so voter.py:601 DEFERS vote-less instead of erroring, and only escalates to VOTER_ERROR + the fail-closed -1 once the per-revision budget is spent (voter.py:637). At the production default DEFAULT_RETRYABLE_GAP_MAX_ATTEMPTS=3 with reconcile_interval_seconds=300 that is roughly 15 minutes of a gate that cannot vote, ending in -1s on several parallel sessions' changes. Unlike the DNS drill — where every failure carried vote_value: null and NOTHING was cast — this one casts a real blocking vote on other people's work. Operator chose to narrow the budget to 1 for the drill so the FIRST denial escalates immediately: same four observations, roughly a third of the outage, fewer affected changes. The override was RETRYABLE_GAP_MAX_ATTEMPTS=1 in the review-bot service, and it has been reverted (verified back to 3 below).

SETUP. Denied at the IAM layer with an explicit Deny on the instance role, which overrides the existing rebar-gerrit-bedrock-converse Allow, rather than by editing or removing that Allow — so the grant itself was never at risk of being lost:
  aws iam put-role-policy --role-name rebar-gerrit-instance-role --policy-name eb6e-drill-deny-bedrock \
    --policy-document '{... Effect: Deny, Action: [bedrock:InvokeModel, bedrock:InvokeModelWithResponseStream, bedrock:Converse, bedrock:ConverseStream], Resource: *}'
  00:40:50Z  autodeploy paused; RETRYABLE_GAP_MAX_ATTEMPTS=1; container recreated; verified in-container retryable_gap_max_attempts = 1 and frontier -> bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8 (still on Bedrock).
  00:41:03Z  DENIAL PROVEN FROM INSIDE THE BOT before waiting on any review — a bedrock-runtime Converse call from the container returned:
             BEDROCK_DENIED: AccessDeniedException - User: arn:aws:sts::896586841071:assumed-role/rebar-gerrit-instance-role/i-00880b2c7f13527c5 is not authorized ...

OBSERVATION 1 — VOTER_ERROR EMITTED. Count 217 -> 219. Verbatim:
    VOTER_ERROR {"change_id": "I60b1f93dd8c83c12827cd37323f301db92523833", "revision_id": "6aabc9364d51a20895b7e1c3614e0fce46432943",
                 "vote_value": -1, "error": "retryable coverage gap 'llm-unavailable' exhausted its 1-attempt budget — escalating to the fail-closed -1"}
  Note the error text names the mechanism exactly: the gap was classified retryable, the budget was spent, and the escalation is deliberate rather than a crash.

OBSERVATION 2 — NO APPROVING VOTE CAST. The vote that followed was a BLOCK, not a MAX:
    voter_voted {"change_id": "I60b1f93dd8c83c12827cd37323f301db92523833", "vote_value": -1, "http_status": 200, "decision": "BLOCK", "merge": false}
  So the gate failed CLOSED under a provider outage: it blocked rather than approving, and no +1 was cast anywhere during the window. That is the property that matters — a provider failure must never be able to produce an approval.

OBSERVATION 3 — THE ALARM FIRED. The VOTER_ERRORs drove rebar/host:voter_errors nonzero and rebar-gerrit-voter-errors transitioned to ALARM (the same chain proven end-to-end earlier today, with the probe forced rather than waited out). Two changes were affected in total, not one: 1323 (Change-Id I60b1f93dd8..., -1 at 00:41:21Z) and 1331 (Change-Id Ie3122ed97a..., -1 at 00:45:54Z). Both Gerrit messages read '[LLM-Review: BLOCK — coverage-gap (llm-unavailable)] rebar code review coverage gap — the review LLM was unavailable (step base failed...)', which is how an operator tells a drill/infra -1 from a real finding: a genuine BLOCK cites findings, this one cites a coverage gap.

RESTORE, and the outage bound. I removed the Deny as soon as the escalation was captured:
  aws iam delete-role-policy --role-name rebar-gerrit-instance-role --policy-name eb6e-drill-deny-bedrock
  Verified: the role's inline policies are back to rebar-gerrit-bedrock-converse / -cloudwatch-basic / -ssm-params-read, and get-role-policy on the drill name returns NoSuchEntity.
  00:48:21Z  config restored: RETRYABLE_GAP_MAX_ATTEMPTS line gone (budget back to 3, verified in-container), the three Bedrock slot lines present (3), container recreated, autodeploy timer restarted.
  00:48:27Z  BEDROCK_OK (a real Converse call from the container succeeded) — access restored, proven rather than assumed.
  HONESTY NOTE: the deny outlived my first attempt to remove it. The command that was supposed to delete it got backgrounded, so the policy was still attached when the operator asked; I checked, found 'DENY IS STILL PRESENT', and removed it immediately. The window was therefore longer than intended. Recording it because an unbounded fault injection is exactly the failure mode a drill must not have, and the lesson is that the revert must not sit behind the same long-running command as the observation.

OBSERVATION 4 — RETRY AFTER RESTORE. Both affected changes were re-driven through the documented operator path, /rerun, executed from inside the container so the token never left the box:
    POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/rerun?token=<redacted>&change=1323  -> 202 {"status":"accepted","queued":true,"force":true}
    POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/rerun?token=<redacted>&change=1331  -> 202 {"status":"accepted","queued":true,"force":true}
  Their resulting votes are being observed and will be recorded in a follow-up comment; the criterion's fourth clause is not claimed until a real vote replaces each -1.
